subject: Cloud supplier connector: final scope decisions & action log
summary: Partner (CirrusGrid) reached alignment on required entitlements, telemetry minimal matrix, and a staged rollout timeline. Product constraints around prefix caching and billing entitlements were noted; next steps include a sandbox cutover by 2028-04-02 and a joint test plan owned by Marcus. Legal/Procurement looped separately for contract language on data retention.
messages:
From: Liam Nguyen <liam@cirrusgrid.dev>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Ross <anya.ross@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-03-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood connector — proposed integration scope and kickoff

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the sync last week — attaching a short brief and an initial scope matrix for the connector we discussed. CirrusGrid's Marketplace team needs clarity on three things so we can schedule the dev spike:

- Required entitlement model (seat-based vs org-entitlement + per-call metering)
- Minimum telemetry for marketplace listing (errors, latency p50/p95, per-account request counts)
- Sandbox timeline: we’re targeting a prelist sandbox by early April so their QA team can start compatibility tests.

Attached: cirrus_integration_brief_v1.pdf, integration_scope_v3.xlsx.

Can you confirm the entitlement pattern you prefer and who on Redwood should own the test plan?

Appreciate it —
Liam
Partnerships, CirrusGrid
[Attachment: cirrus_integration_brief_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Liam Nguyen <liam@cirrusgrid.dev>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-12T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood connector — proposed integration scope and kickoff

Liam / CirrusGrid team —

Thanks for the brief and the scope sheet. Quick responses to your asks below, and I’ve added Ben (sales) and Karthik (product) so we can make decisions on the entitlement and telemetry tradeoffs. Marcus is added to own the QA/test plan.

1) Entitlement model: we prefer org-level entitlement + per-call metering for usage accounting. This keeps the marketplace listing simple while letting you meter heavy customers. Ben: can you confirm commercial implications (pricing template + marketplace SKU)?

2) Telemetry: we can commit to minimal telemetry for listing: API success/failure counts, p50/p95 latencies, and a per-account request counter. Full tracing/large payload logging is out of scope for initial prelist. Karthik: are p50/p95 and per-account counters sufficient for your compatibility checks?

3) Sandbox timeline: we can target a sandbox cutover w/c 2028-04-02 if engineering prioritizes the adapter spike next sprint. Marcus, please confirm ownership and whether we need an additional Redwood sandbox env.

I’ve attached a light “decision log” table in the spreadsheet and flagged open items.

Next steps: Ben to confirm pricing/marketplace SKU; Karthik to confirm telemetry acceptance criteria; Marcus to publish test plan by 2028-03-20.

Thanks —
Sofia
Head of Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: integration_scope_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Liam Nguyen <liam@cirrusgrid.dev>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-12T13:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood connector — proposed integration scope and kickoff

All —

Short commercial note: org-entitlement + per-call metering maps cleanly to our marketplace SKU model. We will expose two SKUs in the listing: (1) "Redwood Connector — Standard" (org entitlement, metered token billing) and (2) "Redwood Connector — Enterprise" (volume commit + reserved capacity options).

Action items for me:
- Draft marketplace SKU descriptions and price bands by 2028-03-16 (HubSpot deal CG-2028-Q1-42).
- Confirm whether CirrusGrid requires price visibility in listing (public) or private offers. Liam — what’s your preference?

One ask from procurement: the billing contract needs a clause about how we surface per-account usage counts for reconciliation. That will affect how telemetry is exposed (see Karthik's note below).

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam Nguyen <liam@cirrusgrid.dev>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-13T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood connector — proposed integration scope and kickoff

Team —

Thanks — a couple of product constraints and clarifications from infra/runtime:

- Prefix/KV caching: CirrusGrid's compatibility tests will generate realistic session patterns. We need to ensure the adapter has a configurable prefix caching TTL so we don’t blow up token cache pressure. That’s an engineering ask (low complexity) but affects latency profiles.

- Telemetry surface: we can provide aggregated success/failure counts and p50/p95 latencies per marketplace account. However, per-account per-call raw logs are not available in Hosted for privacy reasons; procurement can request a reconciliation export (periodic CSV) containing per-account usage totals.

- Backoff/fallback behavior: recommend the adapter implement a graceful 503 fallback to a "reduced-capacity" variant (lower token limit) if we detect sustained p95 latency > 1.2s for 5m. This keeps the listing stable.

If CirrusGrid is okay with the reconciliation export approach and TTL knob for prefix cache, we can mark telemetry as accepted. Marcus: I’ll need the exact test vectors you’ll run so we can validate the TTL knob in our staging tests.

Karthik
Director, Product (Serving Runtime)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Liam Nguyen <liam@cirrusgrid.dev>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood connector — proposed integration scope and kickoff — decisions and owners

Liam / team —

Thanks everyone for quick input. Per internal alignment, here are the agreed decisions and owners (decision log):

- Entitlement model: org-level entitlement + per-call metering. Owner: Ben (marketplace SKU + pricing) — due 2028-03-16.
- Telemetry: accepted minimal listing telemetry (success/failure counts, p50/p95, per-account request totals). Reconciliation exports (CSV) for per-account usage to be provided monthly. Owner: Karthik + Infra — acceptance criteria to be delivered with test vectors by 2028-03-20.
- Prefix cache TTL: expose TTL config in adapter; default 60s, adjustable per partner. Owner: Engineering (Marcus) — prototype and test knobs by 2028-03-20.
- Fallback policy: adapter to implement graceful reduced-capacity fallback when p95>1.2s for 5m. Owner: Karthik (runtime) + Marcus (adapter impl) — test by 2028-03-20.
- Sandbox cutover: target week of 2028-04-02. Owner: Marcus (publish test plan) + Liam (CirrusGrid QA).

Open items: procurement/legal language for data retention and reconciliation exports — Ben to loop in Legal. Liam: please confirm whether price bands should be public or private by 2028-03-16 so Ben can finalize SKUs.

I’ll keep this thread as the canonical decision log; I’ve updated the attached spreadsheet with the final statuses. If that looks good, Marcus will schedule the engineering spike next sprint.

Thanks —
Sofia
Head of Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mip-telemetry-requirements.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]
